screenshots.name: desktop-windlass-practice-coverage.png
screenshots.findings: The two shortcut buttons show the next skill, checked and viewed totals are distinct, and the coverage strip is solid/striped/empty. The five power-family tiles clearly label checked, viewed or unsaved history and earlier setups; text and controls fit.

screenshots.name: desktop-ramp-practice-coverage.png
screenshots.findings: The linear map shows 5 of 18 valid records with explicit category totals; the active Power lost tile is unsaved, matching the invalid-record fixture. Shortcut targets, status labels and the 2/1/2 power-family strip are readable and aligned.

screenshots.name: dark-phone-screw-practice-coverage.png
screenshots.findings: At a 320-pixel viewport, shortcuts and skill tiles stack in one column. Long helper text and category counts wrap cleanly. The bright checked segment, striped viewed segment and empty remainder stay distinct; the active tile and keyboard outline remain visible.

screenshots.name: forced-colors-windlass-practice-coverage.png
screenshots.findings: At a 320-pixel forced-colors viewport, solid black checked coverage, black hatching for viewed solutions and the empty remainder are distinguishable. The current-only solution shortcut displays its unavailable reason, and all status text, borders and the active tile remain readable.

limitations: Screenshots capture the overview and first complete skill family; automated layout and coverage checks inspect all families.
Local native Chromium with software WebGL; no deployed host was tested.
Forced colors was browser emulation; no physical assistive-technology session was performed.
